paper.title: DP-Dueling: Learning from Preference Feedback without Compromising User Privacy

settings.name_in_paper: Finite armed DP-DB (differentially private dueling bandits, D=[K])
unmapped: Utility-based preferences: P(i beats j) = sigma(r(x_i) - r(x_j)) with logistic link (total ordering)
Pure epsilon-differential privacy w.r.t. the preference outcomes o_t (central model)
Regret sums suboptimality of both dueling arms: 2r(x*) - r(a_t) - r(b_t)
settings.definition_quote: At each round $t$, the learner is allowed to actively choose a pair of items $(\a_t,\b_t)$, upon which it gets to see a binary preference feedback $o_t \in \{0,1\}$ ... $o_t \sim \text{Ber}\bign{\sigma(r(\a_t)-r(\b_t))}$ ... In this section, we first address the \dpdb\, problem for finite decision space $\cD = [K]$.

settings.name_in_paper: DP-DB with general d-dimensional decision space
unmapped: Dueling feedback with logistic link on reward differences w*^T(a_t - b_t)
Algorithm uses the minimum-slope constant kappa of the sigmoid
Possibly infinite decision space D subset of B_d(1); discretized by 1/T-net
settings.definition_quote: consider decision space $\cD \subset \cB_d(1)$. Assume any item $\x \in \R^d$ in the decision space is associated with a reward/score parameter $r(\x) = \w^{*\top} \x$ for some unknown $\w^* \in \R^d$.

symbols.Delta_pref_i: preference gap Delta(1,i) = P(1,i) - 1/2 of arm i against the best arm

tuning: binary tree counters with privacy parameter eps/4

source.label: thm:fin
source.quote: For any $T >K$, \algfin ($\cA$)\, is $\eps$-DP and its total regret is upper bounded by $$\cR_T(\cA) = \tO\left( \sum_{i = 2}^K \frac{\log (KT)}{\Delta(1,i)} + \frac{K}{\epsilon} \right).$$

results.notes: Regret type (expected/high-prob) not stated in the theorem; proof is a high-probability-event argument with delta=1/T. Algorithm is also eps-DP.

conditions: holds for some preference matrix P (existential)

source.label: thm:LB_fin
source.quote: Let $K$ and $\epsilon$ be such that $K/\epsilon \le T/2$. For any $(\epsilon,\delta)$ differentially private algorithm $\cA$\, there exist a preference matrix $P$ such that the regret of $\cA$ on $P$ is lower bounded by $$\cR_T(\cA) = \Omega\left( \sum_{i = 2}^K \frac{\log T}{\Delta(1,i)} + \frac{K}{\epsilon} \right),$$

results.notes: Proof only establishes the K/eps term on a constant-gap instance (gap 1/4); the log T/Delta term is attributed to the non-private dueling lower bound. Proof's Lemma requires K/eps <= T/10 and eps <= 1.

symbols.kappa: minimum slope of the sigmoid: inf of sigma'(x^T w) over ||x|| in B_d(1), ||w - w*|| <= 1

tuning: t_0 = 2(C_1 d sqrt(d) + C_2 d sqrt(log(1/delta)))^2 + 16d/kappa^4 (d^2 + log(T/delta))
delta set to 1/(B T ell) in proof

source.label: thm:reg_gen
source.quote: Let $\kappa := \inf ... \dot{\sigma}(\x^\top\theta) > 0 $ and $\w^* \in \cB_d(1)$. Consider any $d$-dimensional decision space $\cD \subseteq \cB_d(1)$. Then for the choice of $t_0 = ...$, and any finite horizon $T$, \cref{alg:gen} is $\epsilon$-DP with regret guarantee at most $O \left(   \frac{d^6\log(dT/\delta) \log({T}\kappa^2/d)}{\kappa \epsilon  } + \frac{ d\sqrt{T}   {\log(T/\delta)}}{\kappa} \right)$.

results.notes: delta is the algorithm's confidence parameter. Proof refers to 'expected regret'. Abstract summarizes as O_tilde(d^6/(kappa eps) + d sqrt(T)/kappa).
